title: Knowledge intake plan
description: The classification of received domain material into the ontology, produced by the domain-analyst agent and consumed by whatever authors the objects. The named producer is domain-analyst; the named consumer is the intake procedure, which reads `state` to decide whether to author and reads each entry to delegate one authoring call. This artifact carries control flow and is validated at the boundary before consumption, so it is a versioned schema rather than prose. It is a plan and not an authority: an entry states the node type and the `ddd` value decided for a construct, and the pairing of the two is checked by knowledge-object.json when the object is authored — duplicating the per-type vocabulary here would give one fact two homes. Gaps are expected content: material arriving from analysis does not carry the retrieval question, the declared out-of-scope, the type parameters, or the identity strategy, and nothing downstream may supply a domain fact the source did not state. An entry with gaps is therefore a classified entry with its gaps named, never a silent completion.

contract_version.description: The contract this instance declares. A consumer selects behaviour on this value and never infers a version from shape.

intake_id.description: Stable identifier for this intake, required for traceability. The caller supplies it: a producer that minted its own identifier could not have its run repeated and compared.

producer.description: The named producer, closed rather than a free string so a document claiming another producer is not an instance of this contract. Two values while one replaces the other: `expand-model` derives the plan from the model deterministically, and `domain-analyst` is the agent it replaces, deprecated and still installed. The agent's entry goes when it is retired, and a consumer that must know which produced a plan reads this field rather than inferring it from shape — the two agree on every field, which is what makes the replacement safe and also what makes the label the only way to tell them apart.

consumer.description: Who reads it. The ingestion procedure reports what became of every construct from this record; nothing else parses it, and a second consumer would be a second place the outcomes are interpreted.

source.description: What material was classified. It travels with the plan because an object derived from material that already existed records the source it was read from — the only record of whether a fact was stated by the business or read out of an artifact, now that a knowledge object carries no status to say so.

description.description: What the material is, in one sentence a reviewer can check against the artifacts named beside it.

artifacts.description: Each artifact the material was read from, by path or by stable reference. Non-empty: a classification whose source cannot be named cannot be reviewed, because nothing states what would have to be re-read to check it.

state.description: The closed outcome the consumer branches on. `classified` means every construct reached a decision, including the ones whose decision is that they have no home in the mapping. `blocked` means the classification could not be reached at all — the material is unintelligible, or a required input is absent.

blocking_reason.description: Why the classification could not be reached. Required on `blocked` and forbidden otherwise: a blocking reason on a successful result says two things at once.

entries.description: One entry per construct the source material holds, whatever became of it. A single list rather than one per outcome, so that what happened to every construct is answerable in one place and the count is checkable against the input — three parallel lists make partial completion a join the reader has to perform.

notes.description: What a reviewer needs that no field above carries — an ambiguity the producer resolved one way and could have resolved another. Prose, and nothing branches on it.

construct.description: What the source material called it. Kept verbatim, so a reviewer can find it in the material rather than guessing which construct an identifier came from.

outcome.description: What happened to this construct, as a closed value a consumer branches on. `classified` — it became a node type and takes an identifier. `unmapped` — the ontology's mapping has no home for it, which is the ordinary answer for stack knowledge and for rationale. `refused` — the model states something the ontology rejects rather than something it lacks: an attribute type outside the closed primitive vocabulary, a step naming an element that resolves to none or to two. A missing fact is a gap and is recorded on a `classified` entry; a wrong fact is a refusal, and nothing is authored from it.

node_type.description: The node type this construct becomes. The vocabulary is the ontology's closed set of six; a plan naming a seventh is rejected at the boundary rather than authored and rejected later.

ddd.description: The DDD construct the entry records, as the value the object's `ddd` field will carry. Required of every classified entry except a `lifecycle`, which is the one node type that *is* a DDD construct rather than carrying one: the ontology maps a state machine to the type itself, so the object has no `ddd` and the contract rejects one. An entry that carried a value here would be naming a field the object may not hold, and the classification that produced it had to invent something to fill it.

origin.description: Copied from the model element this entry classifies, never decided here. The model declares, per element, whether the request stated the fact or the analysis decided it, and `knowledge-object/5` requires the authored object to carry the same value — so this is the hop between them. Without it the authoring step would have to re-decide whether the material said the fact, which is the one judgment a classification may not reopen.

boundary.description: The boundary identifier the authored object will declare. Absent only for a bounded-context boundary, which declares none — that absence is what identifies a partition root, and it is checked when the object is authored.

proposed_id.description: The identifier the object will take, computed from the node type and the boundary by the ontology's id arithmetic rather than allocated. No id allocator exists, and an id that cannot be computed from a path is one a consumer has to look up.

gaps.description: Every fact the node type requires that the source material does not supply. An empty array is a claim that the material is complete for this construct, and it is checkable: the authoring step blocks on a fact it was not given, so a wrongly empty array surfaces there rather than becoming an invention.

reason.description: Why this construct was not classified. Required of `unmapped` and `refused`, and refused of `classified`, which says what happened in its own fields.

allOf.description: `lifecycle` is the node type a state machine *becomes*, so there is no DDD value left to record beside it — and `knowledge-object` rejects `ddd` on one. Requiring it here forced a classification to invent a value the boundary would then refuse.

A construct that became a node type carries what it became; one that did not carries why. Neither carries the other's fields: an unmapped construct with a proposed identifier asserts a home the mapping does not give it.

kind.description: `domain` — only whoever knows the domain can close it, and no capability of this framework may. `authoring` — a step of this framework closes it. Conflating the two makes a report of thirty entries unreadable: a reader cannot tell what is waiting on them from what is waiting on the machine, and stops reading it.

field.description: The field this node type requires and this object does not have, named as the contract names it, in dotted-path form: `attributes`, `identity.attributes`, `attributes[razao_social].max_length`. A validator checks that the path names a field the type would actually require — the schema cannot, because the requirement it excuses is a conditional elsewhere in this document.

why.description: What the domain would have to say to fill it. Required on `kind: domain`; absent on `kind: authoring`, where the field name is the whole content and a required sentence would be written to pass rather than to inform.

question.description: The shared open question this gap instantiates, held once by the analysis rather than copied into every object it blocks. In the reference run nine of twelve open questions bore on more than one construct; without this the same question is restated per file and the restatements drift.

gap.description: The same shape the authored object carries, so a gap crosses the boundary between the two without being restated. Two shapes for one fact is two places for it to drift, and the authoring step copies this entry rather than rebuilding it.
